answer: Deposit-decay identity pricing makes each new agent identity post a refundable deposit that decays like a glacier: slow at first, then nearly flat, so honest long-lived agents recover most of it while mass registrations lose value fast. Enforcement reads deposit age and unlocks perks only as decay completes, forcing attackers to hold capital across thousands of parallel identities rather than pay once. A persistent reef of dormant identities also drains that capital, since each month of waiting costs the attacker umber-valued opportunity and lockup risk.
